an4.123:1.1: “Monks, there are these four types of individuals to be found existing in the world.
an4.123:1.3: “There is the case where an individual, quite secluded from sensuality, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters & remains in the first jhāna: rapture & pleasure born of seclusion, accompanied by directed thought & evaluation.
an4.123:1.4: He savors that, longs for that, finds satisfaction through that.
an4.123:1.5: Staying there—fixed on that, dwelling there often, not falling away from that—then when he dies he reappears in conjunction with the Devas of Brahmā’s Retinue.
an4.123:1.6: The Devas of Brahmā’s Retinue, monks, have a lifespan of an eon.
an4.123:1.7: A run-of-the-mill person having stayed there, having used up all the lifespan of those devas, goes to hell, to the animal womb, to the state of the hungry ghosts.
an4.123:1.8: But a disciple of the Blessed One, having stayed there, having used up all the lifespan of those devas, is unbound right in that state of being.
an4.123:1.9: This, monks, is the difference, this the distinction, this the distinguishing factor, between an educated disciple of the noble ones and an uneducated run-of-the-mill person, when there is a destination, a reappearing.
an4.123:2.1: “Again, there is the case where an individual, with the stilling of directed thoughts & evaluations, enters & remains in the second jhāna: rapture & pleasure born of concentration, unification of awareness free from directed thought & evaluation—internal assurance.
an4.123:2.2: He savors that, longs for that, finds satisfaction through that.
an4.123:2.3: Staying there—fixed on that, dwelling there often, not falling away from that—then when he dies he reappears in conjunction with the Ābhassara [Radiant] devas.
an4.123:2.4: The Ābhassara devas, monks, have a lifespan of two eons.
an4.123:2.5: A run-of-the-mill person having stayed there, having used up all the lifespan of those devas, goes to hell, to the animal womb, to the state of the hungry ghosts.
an4.123:2.6: But a disciple of the Blessed One, having stayed there, having used up all the lifespan of those devas, is unbound right in that state of being.
an4.123:2.7: This, monks, is the difference, this the distinction, this the distinguishing factor, between an educated disciple of the noble ones and an uneducated run-of-the-mill person, when there is a destination, a reappearing.
an4.123:3.1: “Again, there is the case where an individual, with the fading of rapture, remains equanimous, mindful, & alert, senses pleasure with the body, and enters & remains in the third jhāna, of which the noble ones declare, 'Equanimous & mindful, he has a pleasant abiding.’
an4.123:3.2: He savors that, longs for that, finds satisfaction through that.
an4.123:3.3: Staying there—fixed on that, dwelling there often, not falling away from that—then when he dies he reappears in conjunction with the Subhakiṇha [Beautiful Black] devas.
an4.123:3.4: The Subhakiṇha devas, monks, have a lifespan of four eons.
an4.123:3.5: A run-of-the-mill person having stayed there, having used up all the lifespan of those devas, goes to hell, to the animal womb, to the state of the hungry ghosts.
an4.123:3.6: But a disciple of the Blessed One, having stayed there, having used up all the lifespan of those devas, is unbound right in that state of being.
an4.123:3.7: This, monks, is the difference, this the distinction, this the distinguishing factor, between an educated disciple of the noble ones and an uneducated run-of-the-mill person, when there is a destination, a reappearing.
an4.123:4.1: “Again, there is the case where an individual, with the abandoning of pleasure & pain—as with the earlier disappearance of elation & distress—enters & remains in the fourth jhāna: purity of equanimity & mindfulness, neither pleasure nor pain.
an4.123:4.2: He savors that, longs for that, finds satisfaction through that.
an4.123:4.3: Staying there—fixed on that, dwelling there often, not falling away from that—then when he dies he reappears in conjunction with the Vehapphala [Sky-fruit] devas.
an4.123:4.4: The Vehapphala devas, monks, have a lifespan of 500 eons.
an4.123:4.5: A run-of-the-mill person having stayed there, having used up all the lifespan of those devas, goes to hell, to the animal womb, to the state of the hungry ghosts.
an4.123:4.6: But a disciple of the Blessed One, having stayed there, having used up all the lifespan of those devas, is unbound right in that state of being.
an4.123:4.7: This, monks, is the difference, this the distinction, this the distinguishing factor, between an educated disciple of the noble ones and an uneducated run-of-the-mill person, when there is a destination, a reappearing.
an4.123:4.8: “These are four types of individuals to be found existing in the world.”
